# PIP — WhiteKiwi Design System

> PIP is WhiteKiwi's public design system for foundations, semantic tokens, React components, product patterns, and adoption governance. Its thesis is: Quiet canvas. Electric kiwi. Human evidence.

Use the public documentation for implemented behavior and the source repository for exact code. A reference or candidate is not automatically approved or implemented.

## Documentation

- [Usage guide](https://github.com/WhiteKiwi/kiwi-design-system/blob/main/docs/usage.md): Package integration, upgrades, and an agent setup snippet for consuming repositories.
- [Contribution guide](https://github.com/WhiteKiwi/kiwi-design-system/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Shared change ownership, implementation, verification, PRs, and consumer adoption.
- [PIP documentation](https://design.whitekiwi.link/): Implemented foundations, component specimens, patterns, interaction contracts, inventory, and governance.
- [Design guidelines](https://github.com/WhiteKiwi/kiwi-design-system/blob/main/docs/guidelines.md): Canonical visual and interaction rules.
- [Agent design contract](https://github.com/WhiteKiwi/kiwi-design-system/blob/main/DESIGN.md): Compact repository-local implementation contract.
- [Reference base](https://github.com/WhiteKiwi/kiwi-design-system/blob/main/references/README.md): Authoritative sources and adoption stance.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/WhiteKiwi/kiwi-design-system): Tokens, owned React components, public documentation, and deployment source.
- [Semantic tokens](https://github.com/WhiteKiwi/kiwi-design-system/blob/main/packages/tokens/src/theme.css): Light and dark theme roles and interaction states.
- [UI components](https://github.com/WhiteKiwi/kiwi-design-system/tree/main/packages/ui/src): Component source and shared styles.

## Interpretation notes

- PIP separates Foundation, Primitive, Component, Pattern, and Page responsibilities.
- Kiwi green is a brand signal, not a success semantic.
- Static surfaces and navigational surfaces have distinct affordance contracts.
- External registries are implementation references, not visual authority.
- Check installed package versions; GitHub main may contain unreleased changes.
- Improve shared bugs, accessibility issues, and reusable component gaps in the design-system repository; keep product data, business logic, and page composition in the consumer.
- A second real consumer is required only to promote product-specific patterns, not for bug fixes or general-purpose components with a concrete use case.
- Verify packed packages in the consumer, track temporary workarounds, and remove them when adopting the published fix. Repository merge, npm publication, and consumer adoption are separate steps.
